- raid chat bubbles is a setting tied to toggling off party chat bubbles

Melee abilities can reach up to 20 yards range and that's why you can hit a large mob like onyxia from so far away (even while she's flying for example).

author: Oldmana
content:
So what I'm talking about has nothing to do with recycling normal tables. What I'm saying is when you do this
```lua
frameData.frame:Hide()          -- Hide the frame
frameData.frame:SetParent(nil)  -- Detach from UI```
that only makes the frame hidden, but it's still present in memory. This is more of an issue than garbage generation, because these frames will never be released, resulting in a memory leak. The way to solve this is to reuse the frames. This can't be done through Compost because frames aren't normal tables, you'll need to create your own cache. Although what you'd do is a little different, maybe my frame caching for player buffs/debuffs will give you an idea of what I'm talking about: <https://github.com/i2ichardt/HealersMate/blob/main/HMUnitFrame.lua#L855>

author: McPewPew
content:
That's not a bug, that's what you'd expect to happen.
It's not clear what you're trying to do - Do you want to Judge SoW on your target, then keep SoR up and Judge that every time Judgement is off cooldown?
If so, they you'll need to check if your target already has JoW.

Without using other addons, we've got a couple of limits on macros that we need to take into account - 511 character total length limit and no single line over 256 characters.

Run this macro to print the action bar slot your auto attack is on - 
/run for i=1,172 do if IsAttackAction(i) then DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage(i)break end end
(the break means it will stop looking once it's found that it's looking for, otherwise it would carry on to 172 anyway)

Doing this means we can cut most of that code from the main macro, replace the XX in the below macro with the number you just got - 

/run joW=nil;soW=nil;soR=nil;if not IsCurrentAction(XX)then UseAction(XX)end;for i=1,64 do t=UnitDebuff("target",i);if not t then break end;if strfind(t,"y_Righte")then joW=1 break end end
/run for i=1,27 do t=UnitBuff("player",i);if not t then break end;if strfind(t,"y_Righte")then soW=1 end;if strfind(t,"ThunderBolt")then soR=1 end end
/run local cN=CastSpellByName;if not joW then if soW then cN("Judgement")else cN("Seal of Wisdom")end elseif soR then cN("Judgement")else cN("Seal of Righteousness")end

This is 510 characters. CastSpellByName is aliased to "cN" this saves 28 characters over having CastSpellByName written out 4 times and all the variables are kept short for the same reason.
The JoW/SoW texture name is "Spell_Holy_RighteousnessAura",  it's probably possible to make it shorter, but I'd be fairly certain "y_Righte" is unique. 
Things could be shortened further, you could probably get that down to 480 if needed 🤷‍♀️

author: Belthazorg
content:
Some details:
the core out of memory problem is neither from an addon or from hd patch ultra. wow is not releasing ram in certain scenarios that is should, and it adds up, with the big textures from ultra models helping it go over the limit.

So  while it is not the HD patch U fault, it is helping to trigger a preexisting problem.

My addon right now helps a lot since it offloads some of the ram pressure, but we may still have an Out of Memory crash, since it is not directly fixing this preexisting issue.

I'm thinking it could be a consequence of using the 4gb patch in the end, since it could be exposing WoW to this Out of memory error.

I have reverse engineered the problem a whole f**ing lot and I can tell with confidence that a) the above are valid and b) it is potentially fixable once and for all - not there yet but will be eventually.

author: Belthazorg
content:
probed this a lot. dxvk actually helps immensely atm and manages the memory space better - without it OOM is almost instant.
mimalloc could help slightly but the core issue is wow not releasing retained payloads. WoW keeps a full CPU-side copy of every loaded texture's data at owner+0x28C forever — no eviction, no LRU, no cleanup until shutdown. comparing with 1.14 classic client,  (completely different 64bit etc), this happens even there even if this would not cause a OOM crash since it is 64bits.
